generators.carrier: expectation value of the traced Wilson loop on an I x J rectangle of a finite lattice configuration
chi(I,J) = -log( W(I,J) W(I-1,J-1) / ( W(I,J-1) W(I-1,J) ) ) over positive reals
leading strong-coupling (small beta) area-law string tension of the Wilson action; valid only inside the strong-coupling expansion
one-loop coefficient (11/3) N_c - (2/3) N_f as an exact rational

relations.statement: The finite control test for part C checks the plaquette reduction and Wilson/Creutz confinement rows of the finite map.
relations.hypotheses: finite lattice; strong-coupling rows only; no continuum claim

relations.statement: The Creutz ratio is a function of four Wilson-loop expectation values, so each of its four input slots has colour wilson_loop and accepts the output of G_wilson_loop.
relations.hypotheses: all four Wilson-loop expectation values are strictly positive

relations.statement: G_strong_coupling_area_law yields a string_tension_estimate only within the strong-coupling expansion at finite lattice spacing; it carries no statement about the a -> 0 limit or about weak coupling.
relations.hypotheses: beta small enough that the strong-coupling series applies

relations.statement: F002.S001 admits no book and its Pontryagin inventory is not a bridge theorem; any step from finite strong-coupling rows to a continuum mass gap is an open bridge, not a derivation.
relations.hypotheses: none; this is a scope restriction, not a theorem

lemmas.statement: For strictly positive reals W1,W2,W3,W4, -log(W1*W2/(W3*W4)) = -(log W1 + log W2 - log W3 - log W4); this is the algebraic form of the Creutz ratio and makes no confinement claim.
lemmas.lean_skeleton:
theorem creutz_log_split (W1 W2 W3 W4 : ℝ) (h1 : 0 < W1) (h2 : 0 < W2) (h3 : 0 < W3) (h4 : 0 < W4) : -Real.log (W1 * W2 / (W3 * W4)) = -(Real.log W1 + Real.log W2 - Real.log W3 - Real.log W4) := by
  rw [Real.log_div (mul_pos h1 h2).ne' (mul_pos h3 h4).ne', Real.log_mul h1.ne' h2.ne', Real.log_mul h3.ne' h4.ne']
  ring

near_misses.claim: The strong-coupling area law of the Wilson action implies confinement (a mass gap) in the continuum limit a -> 0.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: R_strong_coupling_scope: the strong-coupling expansion holds only at small beta / finite spacing; the continuum limit is at weak coupling, outside its domain, and the target explicitly withholds the continuum claim.

near_misses.claim: Positivity of beta0 (asymptotic freedom) implies confinement.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: beta0 is a one-loop ultraviolet perturbative coefficient; confinement is an infrared non-perturbative property, and no relation listed here connects the colours beta_coefficient and string_tension_estimate.

near_misses.claim: Citing F002.S001 (Pontryagin inventory) supplies the bridge from the finite certificate to the continuum mass gap.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: R_bridge_open: README.md admits no book, GAP-F002-S001-001 is open, and named_adjoining.yaml says the inventory is not a bridge theorem.

near_misses.claim: The passing part C control test proves confinement beyond the strong-coupling formulae.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: R_part_c_check: the test only checks the finite plaquette-reduction and Wilson/Creutz rows; a finite check cannot certify a continuum or weak-coupling statement.

open_obligations: Continuum (a -> 0) mass-gap claim: no finite certificate or admitted source supplies it; remains open.
Non-perturbative behaviour at weak coupling as the spacing goes to zero: not derivable from strong-coupling formulae; remains open.
F002.S001 bridge theorem: shelf is empty (README.md admits no book, GAP-F002-S001-001 open); cited only as an open bridge.
